steps.label: Do Now: Parts of a Packet (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Parts of a Packet (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is a large file split into many small packets, and not sent as one piece?Show the answer

If one small packet is lost or damaged, only that packet has to be sent again, and packets can share the network with other traffic.

Recap of 2.1 Data Transmission. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2025, Question 3(a). Data is split into packets before it is transmitted across a network. A packet has three sections. Give the name of each section, and an example of what is stored in that section.

Total: 6 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: the parts of a packet

steps.text: A similar question. A packet is being sent from a laptop to a printer. Name the part of the packet that holds the page to print, and give one thing at the very end of the packet.
A packet has three parts, in this order: the header, then the payload, then the trailer.
The header goes first because routers read it to send the packet the right way. So it holds addresses and the packet number.
steps.visual: header: where from, where to, which packet

steps.text: The middle part carries what is actually being sent. Here, part of the page to print: that is the payload.
The last part tells the receiver the packet has ended and holds data to check for errors: the trailer.
steps.visual: trailer: end of packet, error checking data

steps.text: Now do the same for the question: name each section in order, and give one thing each section stores.
steps.visual: name it, then say what it holds

steps.label: Do Now: Serial Full-Duplex (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Serial Full-Duplex (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can full-duplex send data both ways at the same time, when half-duplex cannot?Show the answer

Full-duplex has a path for each direction, so the two directions never have to take turns.

Recap of 2.1. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2025, Question 3(b)(i). Packets can be sent across a network using different methods of data transmission.

items.prompt: Explain how data is transmitted using serial full-duplex.
scheme: Data is sent one bit at a time
down a single wire
Data can be sent in both directions
at the same time
items.guidance: One mark for each point. "Both directions" earns its mark only with "at the same time" as a separate mark: both directions alone is 1 mark. "Down a single wire" needs the idea of one wire or channel.
items.modelAnswer: Data is sent one bit at a time down a single wire. Data can travel in both directions at the same time.

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: explaining a transmission method

steps.text: A similar question. Explain how data is transmitted using parallel simplex.
steps.visual: two words: two halves of the answer

steps.text: Split the name. The first word (serial or parallel) says how many bits go at once. The second (simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex) says which directions.
Parallel: several bits are sent at the same time, down several wires.
steps.visual: parallel: many bits at once, many wires

steps.text: Simplex: data goes in one direction only.
Put the two halves together, one point per mark: several bits at the same time, down several wires, in one direction only.
Now do the same for serial full-duplex: say how many bits go at once and down how many wires, then which directions and when.

steps.label: CPU and Microprocessors
steps.content:
3.1 Computer Architecture

CPU and Microprocessors

Year 10

  • Today: what the CPU does, and why every computer needs one.
  • What a microprocessor is, and why devices use them.
  • Why a program and its data are stored in the same memory.
Think → Pair → ShareA phone, a washing machine and a games console are very different. What job might all three need done inside them?Show the answer

They all take data in, work on it, and give a result out. Something inside each one has to do that work.

steps.label: What Does the CPU Do?
steps.content:
What Does the CPU Do?

Think → Pair → ShareYou type 12 + 30 into a calculator app and the screen shows 42. Predict: which part of the computer worked out 42, and why could it not do it before you typed?Show the worked answer

The CPU (central processing unit) worked it out. It needs the data first: it can only process what has been input.

  • CPU stands for central processing unit.
  • The CPU processes instructions and data that are input.
  • It does this so that the result can be output.
  • Processing means calculating, comparing and deciding.
  • Every program is a list of instructions the CPU carries out.
Input
You type 12 + 30
→
Process (CPU)
The CPU adds 12 and 30
→
Output
The screen shows 42
Input
A barcode is scanned
→
Process (CPU)
The CPU looks up the price
→
Output
The screen shows the total

steps.label: Predict: Which Step Is Processing?
steps.content:
Predict: Which Step Is Processing?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do we call it the "central" processing unit?Show the answer

All the processing in the computer goes through it: it sits in the middle, between the input and the output.

items.prompt: A games console: you press jump, the console works out where the character lands, and the screen shows the jump. Which step is the CPU processing?
options: Working out where the character lands
items.explain: Pressing jump is input and the screen is output. Working out where the character lands is the CPU processing the data.

items.prompt: Why can the CPU not show the result before the data is input?
options: The screen is switched off until then
It has no data to process yet
The CPU only works when it is cool
items.explain: The CPU processes the data that is input. With no data, there is nothing to work on, so no result to output.

steps.label: Activity 1: Input, Process, Output
steps.content:
Activity 1: Input, Process, Output

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can one device have two process steps in a row?Show the answer

The CPU may need to do more than one piece of work, such as compare a reading and then decide, before it outputs anything.

Label each step of a device. One check per device, and a mistake means it does not count. Then the sensor systems, then find the missing step.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Purpose of the CPU
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Purpose of the CPU

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "the brain of the computer" not enough to earn a mark?Show the answer

It does not say what the CPU does. The marks are for the job: processing data and carrying out instructions.

Adapted from Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2022, Question 5(a). Harriet has a computer. The computer has a central processing unit (CPU).

items.prompt: Explain the purpose of the CPU.
scheme: It processes data
It processes or executes instructions
It carries out calculations
It carries out logical operations
items.guidance: Any two different points from the list, one mark each. "It is the brain of the computer" earns no mark. "Processes data and instructions" in one sentence can earn both marks.
items.modelAnswer: It processes data and executes instructions.

steps.label: What Is a Microprocessor?
steps.content:
What Is a Microprocessor?

Think → Pair → ShareA washing machine needs to check the water temperature and switch a heater on. Predict: why would its maker use one small chip, not a whole computer?Show the worked answer

One chip is small, cheap and uses little power, and it can still do the processing the machine needs.

  • A microprocessor is an integrated circuit (one chip).
  • It can perform many of the functions of a CPU.
  • It is small, cheap and uses little power.
  • Found in washing machines, drones, security lights and phones.
  • It still processes data input to it, so a result can be output.
Input
Temperature sensor sends a reading
→
Process (CPU)
Microprocessor compares it with 30
→
Output
Signal to switch the heater on
Sensor
An input device that measures something, such as temperature or distance, and sends the reading to the microprocessor.

steps.label: Exam Question: A Drone
steps.content:
Exam Question: A Drone

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "a small computer" not a full answer?Show the answer

It does not say what it is made of or what it does. The answer needs one chip that does the CPU's work.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2026, Question 3(b)(ii). A drone is used to search for lost animals. The drone has a built-in system to stop it from crashing into objects, for example a tree. The system uses sensors and a microprocessor.

items.prompt: State what is meant by a microprocessor.
scheme: An integrated circuit (chip) that can perform many of the functions of a CPU
items.guidance: One mark for the idea of a single integrated circuit or chip that does the work of (many functions of) a CPU, or that processes data. "A small computer" alone earns no mark.
items.modelAnswer: An integrated circuit that can perform many of the functions of a CPU.

steps.label: Exam Question: A Washing Machine
steps.content:
Exam Question: A Washing Machine

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must the system keep checking, and not check once?Show the answer

The water keeps cooling or heating, so a reading from a minute ago may already be wrong.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2021, Question 9(b). A washing machine uses sensors and a microprocessor to control the washing cycle of clothes. Use input, process and output to plan your answer.

items.prompt: Describe how the sensor and the microprocessor are used to make sure the water remains at 30 °C.
scheme: The sensor sends data to the microprocessor
The data is converted from analogue to digital (using an ADC)
The data is compared to the stored value (of 30)
If the data is below 30 the microprocessor sends a signal to the heater to heat the water up (or add hot water)
If the data is above 30 the microprocessor sends a signal to turn the heater off (or add cold water)
An actuator is used to turn the heater on or off (or to add water)
If the data is 30 no action is taken
It is a continuous process
items.guidance: Six from the list, one mark each. The sensor must send data to the microprocessor: a sensor that "controls" or "decides" earns no mark, as the microprocessor does the comparing. "Turns the heater on" needs the condition (below 30) for its mark.
items.modelAnswer: The temperature sensor sends data to the microprocessor. The microprocessor compares the data to the stored value of 30. If it is below 30, it sends a signal to turn the heater on. If it is above 30, it sends a signal to turn the heater off. If it is 30, no action is taken. This repeats continuously.

steps.label: Why Store the Program in Memory?
steps.content:
Why Store the Program in Memory?

Think → Pair → ShareThe memory below holds a program and some numbers. The input is 10. Predict: what will the program output, and why is address 4 never used?Show the worked answer

17. The CPU runs addresses 0, 1, 2 and 3 in turn: 10, then 10 + 7 = 17, then outputs 17, then stops. Address 4 comes after STOP, so it is never reached.

  • Instructions and data are stored in the same memory.
  • The CPU runs the instructions one after another, in order.
  • Change the program or the data in memory and the computer does a new job, with no new hardware.
  • This is the stored program idea. Every computer you use works this way.
AddressStored in memory
0INPUT
1ADD 5
2OUTPUT
3STOP
440
57

Purple: instructions. Yellow: data.

steps.label: Predict: Change the Memory
steps.content:
Predict: Change the Memory

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does storing the program in memory mean one computer can do many different jobs?Show the answer

To change the job, you only change what is in memory. The hardware stays the same.

The same memory as before: INPUT, ADD 5, OUTPUT, STOP, then 40 and 7 in addresses 4 and 5.

items.prompt: Address 5 is changed from 7 to 20. The input is 10. What is output now?
items.explain: ADD 5 adds whatever is stored in address 5. It now holds 20, so 10 + 20 = 30. The program did not change, only the data.

items.prompt: Address 1 is changed from ADD 5 to ADD 4. The input is 10. What is output now?
items.explain: ADD 4 adds what is stored in address 4, which is 40. 10 + 40 = 50. Changing one instruction in memory changed what the computer does.

steps.label: Activity 2: Run the Program
steps.content:
Activity 2: Run the Program

Think → Pair → ShareWhy should you predict before you press Run?Show the answer

Running it first shows the answer. Predicting first shows whether you can follow the program yourself.

Predict first, then run it one instruction at a time to see why. Four levels; a wrong prediction means the round does not count.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Stored Program Concept (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Stored Program Concept (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must the instructions be run in order, one at a time?Show the answer

Each instruction may use the result of the one before, so doing them out of order would give the wrong result.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 8(a). A computer system uses the stored program concept.

items.prompt: Describe what is meant by the stored program concept.
scheme: Instructions and data are stored in the same (main) memory
Instructions are fetched and executed in order (one after another, in sequence)
items.guidance: One mark for each point. "Run one after another" or "in order" earns the second mark. "Programs are stored on the computer" alone earns no mark: it must say instructions and data share the same memory.
items.modelAnswer: Instructions and data are stored in the same memory. The instructions are run one after another.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Stored Program Concept (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Stored Program Concept (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can the same 2 marks appear in two different papers?Show the answer

The stored program idea does not change, so the mark scheme points stay the same.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2022, Question 1(d). A train station has a ticket machine. The computer in the ticket machine uses the stored program concept.

scheme: Data and instructions are stored in the same memory
and can only be fetched (taken) one at a time
items.guidance: One mark for each point. The second mark needs the idea that instructions are taken from memory one at a time, or run one after another.
items.modelAnswer: Data and instructions are stored in the same memory, and are taken from memory one at a time.
